findings.summary: Nothing in the change requests a v1 report from the worker seat, so the Definition-of-Done clause 'Worker turns emit a valid v1 report' is unmet; combined with the now-strict ingress this makes every real worker turn a protocol failure. `worker_turn` sends `state['pending_prompt']` (the coordinator's `next_prompt`) verbatim with no report instruction appended, and the worker seat is a generic agent from agents.yaml (`config/ronin-lines.json` seats are `opencode-*`, driven only by that prompt) with no persona requesting the schema. `parse_worker_envelope` then treats prose-without-a-report as `ReportProtocolError`, which `worker_turn` converts to TERMINAL_FAULT. The spec's scope line explicitly contemplates changing worker prompts to request the report, and that in-repo lever was not used.

Structural test criterion 6 is not implemented: no structural guard pins the ordinary orchestration path to the structured-report decoder/projection. `project_control` is exercised only in the standalone `tests/test_work_report.py`; no test or conformance check fails if the graph stops routing through the decoder/projection, and the repo's own structural-guard idioms (`scripts/check_supervisor_conformance.py`, `tests/source_tools.executable_source`, the `ast`-walk in `tests/test_arbiter.py:370`) were not extended to E4a. The `# Structural guard (E4a)` comment at goal_line.py:636 is prose, not a guard. Criterion 6 is listed separately from criterion 4, so the existing behavioural conflicting-prose tests do not discharge it.

The explicit attachment size limit is bypassed on the one path that carries unbounded legacy text: `parse_worker_envelope` assigns `report['prose_attachment']` after `decode_report` has already run, so `ATTACHMENT_CONTENT_MAX_CHARS` (work_report.py:74, enforced only inside `_prose_attachment`) never applies to carried-forward prose. A seat returning a valid `report` plus a multi-megabyte `text` yields a report whose attachment exceeds the declared bound and is persisted by `write_worker_report`, contradicting the spec's 'attachment size limits must be explicit in code and reject, rather than truncate, oversized content'.

The mechanical product-consistency check between the implementation and review commits could not be executed: this reviewer has read-only file inspection and no shell/Git access, so `git diff --exit-code 85a9738d93b9b0a63c5b8520f4d3b2f8b1f87d2e b04be1309e38967864e9b49cc35bb1c91bdded75 -- . ':(exclude).dev-dispatch'` was not run. Consistency was instead checked by inspecting the worktree: the only `.dev-dispatch/` content is the reserved namespace (spec, implement handoff, feedback index, RC review artifact) and no product file shows evidence of a materialization-time edit. This note records the unrun check, not a detected divergence; the deterministic seal verifies the actual Git HEAD independently.
